gen-dafont-blockletter-general-sans: Pencil-sketched and precise, Blockletter carries a squat, tall-bellied midsection above General Sans, whose sans-serif strokes keep a steady pressure throughout. Paragraphs glide along, because every bend is smooth and unobstructed.
gen-dafont-bloody-manrope: Commanding and a bit gory, Bloody swells into big round lowercase bowls. Manrope, a sans, spins thin, same-width lines with bright gaps at every curve, so paragraphs flow with little resistance.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-satoshi: Extra-wide spacing gives Bushcraft its artistic sprawl, with curves that never shift in weight. Satoshi, a sans with a soaring x-height and a wide-open e, is what makes the pair approachable.
gen-dafont-disorder-work-sans: Disorder looks raw and chaotic, its big high-x-height lowercase letters set well apart with no swelling where curves meet stems. Work Sans stays modern underneath, so a slightly larger body size wouldn't hurt.
gen-dafont-college-fs-asap: Dynamic and authoritative, College gives its curves the full strength of its straight stems, and its counters are big. Asap, a sans-serif, keeps its c forms as open arcs and its body height close to the capitals.
gen-dafont-dogica-fs-epilogue: Dogica is heavy and commanding, with wide tracking and a clear opening at the end of every curve. And Epilogue's wire-like monoline skeleton and curvy, unclamped letters are the real draw.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-fs-fira-sans: Early GameBoy stretches out playfully, its brush-like strokes showing slight pressure variation and a skyward x-height line. Shrink Early GameBoy and its open tracking loses its swagger beside Fira Sans.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-archivo: Cast-iron swagger: Edo SZ gives its lowercase the stature of capitals, with stems and arcs in lockstep. Archivo, a sans with curves that open outward, is what makes the pair editorial and approachable.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-fs-public-sa: Public Sans reads trustworthy and hefty, with broad open counters, while Eight Bit Dragon strides across widely separated letters. Both carry a big lowercase body, and that shared stature is the draw.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-fs-supreme: Electroharmonix is striking and commanding, breaking each word into single letters with open-handed curves in every round character. Supreme, a sans with a thick middle strip of text, can take a modest bump in size.
